title: Confirming a trip 500s on Postgres (FK order) and timestamps shift by session timezone
description: Prod /intake/confirm raised ForeignKeyViolation days_base_place_id_fkey: without ORM relationships SQLAlchemy inserted days before places. SQLite tests passed because FKs weren't enforced. Also found via local Postgres: aware datetimes written to TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE were converted through session timezone, breaking geocoding retry timing. Fix: flush parents before children in create_trip, confirm_draft, delete_trip; utcnow() returns naive UTC; tests enforce SQLite FKs and can run on Postgres via TEST_DATABASE_URL.
close_reason: Fixed; 36 tests pass on SQLite (FKs on) and Postgres.

title: Lock backend dependencies so Render builds match tested versions
description: requirements.txt used open ranges, so a Render rebuild on 2026-09-23 picked up sqlmodel 0.0.47, which rejects naive datetimes and broke every insert on prod. sqlmodel is now pinned, but everything else still floats. Add a lockfile (pip-tools/uv pip compile -> requirements.lock or pinned requirements.txt) used by both the local venv and Render's buildCommand, and document how to upgrade deliberately. Separately decide whether to move to aware datetimes/NaiveDatetime annotations so newer sqlmodel works.

title: Vague base places pin to wrong continent; use chosen hotel as a day's location
description: Prod: 'Central France' pinned to Ville de France, Goiânia, Brazil. Cause: locate_city's settlement-anywhere fallback has no proximity check. Knock-on: hotel options for those days were rejected by the 40 km-from-base guard (base in Brazil), so no option pins. Fix: anywhere-fallback only accepted if in trip countries or within ~1500 km of the trip's other located cities; area-in-countries tried before anywhere. Option/chosen places get retried pins (board + worker share one locator). Map uses a chosen hotel's location for a day's pin and the route when available. Migration resets city pins, clears cache, and re-queues unpinned option places.
close_reason: City fallback now requires trip countries or <=1500 km from trip's other pinned cities (cities pinned in trip order); area-in-countries tried before anywhere. Option and chosen places are retried through the shared locator (board background + worker), with a research map_query field and a leading-town settlement fallback for descriptive names (Clermont-Ferrand city centre..., Blois–Chambord loop...). Map uses a chosen pinned hotel as its base place's pin and in the route. Data migration clears cache, resets city pins, re-queues unpinned options. Regression tests for Central France->Brazil and Holly's Clermont stay; 83 tests on SQLite and Postgres.

title: Add plans to a day: find ideas with AI or add manually
description:
Today each day gets one starter activity gap ('What to do in Lisbon on May 2'). Choosing an option answers it, and there's no way to add a second plan, ask for something specific, or type in a plan you already know.

Goal: a day can hold any number of plans, added two ways from the Day tab's 'Plans for the day' section via an 'Add a plan' button.

1. Find ideas (AI): the traveler says what they want ('dinner near our hotel', 'a morning walk', 'something rainy-day friendly') and optionally a time of day. Creates a new day-scoped activity Gap whose prompt is their request, opens the compare drawer, and runs research with that prompt (existing worker, choose/hide/find more/change all apply). Research context should include the day's already-planned items and chosen stay so ideas fit around them.
2. Add it yourself: short form (name, time of day morning/afternoon/evening/any, optional address or link, notes) that creates an Activity directly with created_by = user. Address/link lookup for a map pin within 40 km of the day's city, same guard as research options.

Also:
- Show plans grouped or ordered by time of day (PRD's morning/afternoon/evening slots); allow reordering.
- Edit and remove a plan. Removing an AI-chosen plan offers to reopen its options; removing a manual one just deletes it (or soft-deletes once travelplanner-266 lands).
- The starter 'What to do' gap stays as the empty-day prompt; once a day has any plan, don't count it as missing.
- Tests: multiple plans per day, custom-prompt research context, manual add with and without a pin, removal paths, privacy.
close_reason: Merged PR #2 into master with share link and deployed 2026-09-16. Add a plan (Find ideas request research with day plans + chosen stay context, or Add it yourself with best-effort pin), time-of-day ordering, reorder, edit, remove (reopen vs delete), starter gap only counts while day empty, Add a plan is the single entry point for day plans. Python review found removed requests still ran paid research; fixed with cancel + worker backstop and tests. 101 tests on SQLite and Postgres; migration checked on Postgres.

title: Geocoding pins cities on unrelated POIs (e.g. Paris -> 'Victor Paris' shop in Edinburgh)
description:
Holly's TdF trip (prod trip a9b1bca9-855c-4493-8827-6f046306aa3a) route loops back to Edinburgh on the last day. Cause: backend/app/geocoding.py _queries_for appends the trip's first destination as free text. When that destination is a city, Nominatim matches POIs/streets containing both words. Verified live 2026-09-16:
- 'Paris, Edinburgh' -> Victor Paris, Dundee Street, Edinburgh (wrong city)
- 'London, Edinburgh' -> The Duke of Edinburgh pub, London (right city by luck)
- 'Leeds, Edinburgh' -> Edinburgh Place, Leeds (right city by luck)
- 'Lille, Edinburgh' -> no match, fell back to 'Lille'

Fix plan:
1. Query Nominatim with featureType=settlement (city/town/village only) and drop free-text destination context; optionally pass countrycodes derived from trip destinations.
2. Sanity-check result addresstype/class before accepting.
3. Tests with fake fetcher asserting params, plus a regression case for 'Paris' with an Edinburgh-first trip.
4. Data cleanup (migration or one-off script run on Render): delete geocode_cache rows whose query contains a comma context, reset lat/lng/precision/geocoded_at on city places so the board re-geocodes. Confirm the TdF trip's Paris pin moves to France.
close_reason: Fixed: geocoding no longer appends destinations as free text. Cities are looked up as featureType=settlement limited to the trip's country codes (resolved per destination, e.g. Scotland->gb), then settlement anywhere, then administrative areas within trip countries; only boundary/place results accepted, so shops/buildings/roads never match. Cache keyed by structured params and stores category/country_code. Migration clears old cache and resets city pins so trips re-geocode on next board load. Regression test for Edinburgh->Paris; migration verified on Postgres and SQLite; live Nominatim located Edinburgh, Leeds, London, Lille, Paris correctly and left Douro Valley unpinned.

title: Soft-delete trips with deleted_at (trash with restore)
description:
Today DELETE /trips/{id} hard-deletes the trip and all children (days, places, gaps, candidates, sources, research jobs, members); no undo. Replace with soft delete.

Plan:
- Migration: add trips.deleted_at (nullable naive-UTC timestamp, indexed).
- DELETE /trips/{id} sets deleted_at = utcnow() instead of removing rows (owner-only, as now).
- Every trip read path excludes deleted trips: list_trips, get_member_trip (404 when deleted), board, days, research start, intake confirm results, worker build_context (fail job if trip deleted), geocoding (skip), future share link (deleted trips never public).
- Trash: GET /trips?deleted=true lists the user's deleted trips; POST /trips/{id}/restore clears deleted_at. Web: 'Recently deleted' section on the trip list with Restore; delete confirm copy says it can be restored for N days.
- Purge: after 30 days, a scheduled job (worker loop or Render cron) hard-deletes children-first with per-table flushes (reuse current delete_trip logic).
- Tests on SQLite (FKs on) and Postgres: deleted trips hidden everywhere, restore works, strangers can't restore, purge removes old ones only, queued research on a deleted trip fails cleanly.
close_reason: Merged and deployed 2026-09-17.

title: Saved places: pin spots to the map without assigning a day
description:
A trip-wide bucket of places the traveler wants on the map but hasn't scheduled: coffee shops, parks, bakeries, viewpoints, shops. Like the TDF planner's places.csv layer.

Data model already mostly supports it: Place is trip-scoped with kind (coffee, food, sight, shop, ...) and nullable coordinates, and Gap.day_id is nullable for trip-wide gaps. Likely additions: a Place.saved flag (or status: saved | scheduled), optional note/tags, and which city it's near.

Scope ideas:
- Board: 'Saved places' tab listing them, grouped by city and kind; map layer toggles per kind (the layer toggles deferred from the planning board epic).
- Add a place by name/link (geocoded server-side, or picked from research results), with a note.
- Research: 'Find coffee shops near our Lisbon base' as a trip-wide gap whose accepted options become saved places, not scheduled activities.
- Later: move a saved place onto a day (becomes an Activity), and show nearby saved places on the Day tab.
- Share link shows saved places as an optional map layer.
close_reason: Merged and deployed 2026-09-17.

title: Verify Clerk token azp (authorized party) in API auth
description:
Hardening. backend/app/auth.py decode_clerk_token verifies RS256 signature, expiry, and issuer, but not the azp claim. Clerk recommends checking azp against the app's allowed frontend origins so a token for this Clerk instance obtained via another site is rejected.

Plan: add AUTHORIZED_PARTIES setting (comma-separated, default from CORS_ORIGINS), reject tokens whose azp is present and not in the list with 401. Tests: valid azp passes, foreign azp 401, missing azp behavior decided explicitly. Update Render env when custom domain lands (travelplanner-bgi).
close_reason: API now rejects Clerk tokens whose azp names a site outside AUTHORIZED_PARTIES (defaults to CORS_ORIGINS, so no Render env change), matching Clerk's authorizedParties rule (azp checked when present). Also requires exp, iat, sub claims. 9 new tests sign real RS256 tokens with a local key: our origins pass, foreign azp/wrong issuer/expired/missing sub/wrong key get 401, plus an end-to-end /me check.

title: PDF export of a trip's itinerary, for offline/no-signal use
description:
PRD section 10 already scopes 'Calendar export, PDF' as Later; this is the PDF half. Motivation: cell service isn't guaranteed while traveling, so a downloaded PDF (or print-to-PDF) of the itinerary is a real fallback the app doesn't have yet -- the share link (app/routers/share.py, web/src/pages/SharedTrip.tsx) is the closest existing thing but still needs connectivity to load.

Likely the cheapest path: a print-friendly stylesheet on the existing read-only SharedTrip view (or a dedicated print route) that a browser's own 'Print to PDF' can use, rather than a server-side PDF renderer -- avoids a new dependency and keeps one source of truth for the itinerary layout. Should include days, lodging, activities, transit, confirmation codes/booking links as plain text (a link is useless offline, but the text of what was booked isn't). Calendar export (.ics) is separate scope, not this bead.
acceptance_criteria: Traveler can produce a PDF (via print or a direct download) containing the full itinerary -- days, lodging, activities, transit, confirmation details -- readable without any network connection once saved.

title: Weather forecast/climate context and a packing list
description:
Show weather for the trip and generate a packing list from it.

Real open question baked into the feature itself: actual forecasts are only reliable ~10-14 days out, but most trips get planned months ahead. So this likely needs two modes: seasonal climate normals (avg highs/lows, typical rain) for a trip that's far off, switching to a real forecast once the trip is close enough for one to exist. Needs a weather data source/API decision (not yet chosen; nothing in the codebase touches weather today).

Packing list: derive from temperature range, precipitation likelihood, and trip.interests/activity mix (e.g. 'hiking' + cold nights -> layers; beach + hot -> sun protection), not a generic one-size list. Should be editable by hand afterward like everything else in this app (agent proposes, traveler owns the result), not a locked checklist.

Scope questions to settle before building: per-city or per-day granularity given multi-city trips; where it lives in the UI (new board tab vs. a section on Overview); whether it's agent-generated (costs money, more tailored) or a simpler rules-based list off the weather data alone.
acceptance_criteria: Trip board shows weather context (forecast or seasonal normals depending on how far out the trip is) and an editable packing list a traveler can check off.

title: Let interests be added after intake, not just set once
description:
Trip.interests (app/models.py) is set once at intake confirm (app/routers/intake.py) and then read-only forever after: every research job's ResearchContext.interests (worker/__main__.py -> app/agents/research.py _format_context) pulls straight from the trip row, but there's no endpoint or board UI to change it once the trip exists. A traveler who realizes mid-planning 'oh, we're into hiking too' has no way to feed that into future research jobs short of editing the DB.

Needs: a small edit affordance on the board (e.g. near the trip title/status pill) and a PATCH-style endpoint on trips.py to update the list. Same gap likely applies to Trip.destinations, which is also set once at confirm and never editable -- worth deciding together whether this covers both or just interests.
acceptance_criteria: Traveler can add (and remove) interest tags from the board after the trip is created; the next research job for that trip reflects the updated list.

title: Investigate: chosen lodging sometimes doesn't get a map pin
description:
A chosen lodging option sometimes never shows as its own dot on the trip map -- it falls back to showing just the city's pin instead.

How it's supposed to work (traced, not yet reproduced against real data -- local dev.db has no lodging rows to test against):
- TripMap.tsx only draws a lodging as its own marker if its Place has lat/lng (hasCoords/pinned check). Without coords, the day's 'stop' just uses the city's pin and the lodging is visually indistinguishable from a plain city day.
- Places get pinned two ways: (1) the research agent can supply lat/lng directly in its candidate response, but SYSTEM_PROMPT (app/agents/research.py) deliberately tells it 'only give coordinates when a source provides them or the place is a well-known landmark' -- so this is rare for a hotel. (2) Passive best-effort geocoding via app.geocoding._locate_options, triggered by app.routers.board.get_board's background.add_task(locate, trip.id) whenever the board loads and any place still needs_lookup(). This calls locate_option() against Nominatim with the hotel's name/address/map_query, biased near the base city -- Nominatim is tuned for addresses and settlements, not individual business POIs, so it can plausibly fail silently for many real hotel names (falls through to 'no nearby settlement or area found', logged but not surfaced to the user).
- Note: app.routers.choices.choose_candidate (choosing a researched option) does NOT itself trigger background.add_task(locate, ...) -- only app.routers.choices.add_lodging (the manual 'add it yourself' path) does. A chosen researched candidate only gets picked up passively the next time the board loads and finds it in pending_lookup, so there could also be a timing gap right after choosing.

To actually diagnose next time it happens: query that trip's Place row for the lodging (SELECT lat, lng, precision, geocoded_at, address, name FROM places WHERE id=<place_id>) -- geocoded_at set but lat NULL means Nominatim was tried and found nothing (the likely case); geocoded_at NULL means it was never even attempted (a background.add_task gap); check server logs for 'locating option ... failed' or 'no nearby settlement or area found' for that place name.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause confirmed against a real Place row (Nominatim miss vs. never attempted vs. something else); fix or accepted limitation documented.

title: Trip status: dreaming/planning/booked/done never changes after creation
description: TRIP_STATUSES = (dreaming, planning, booked, done) exists in app/routers/trips.py and the board shows a status pill (STATUS_LABELS in web/src/lib/api.ts), but nothing ever transitions it: every trip is created with status='planning' in app/routers/intake.py's confirm_draft and there's no endpoint or UI to change it afterward. Needs at minimum a manual status picker on the board; consider later whether any transition should be automatic (e.g. 'booked' once lodging + all activities have a chosen option, 'done' after the trip's end_date passes).
acceptance_criteria: Traveler can change a trip's status from the board; the pill reflects it; new status persists.

title: Holistic trip-plan review: pacing, geography, and balance feedback
description: On-demand 'Review my plan' action on the board. Sends the confirmed plan (days, activities, lodging, transit) to an agent that judges the whole trip rather than one gap at a time: pacing/density (crammed or suspiciously empty days), geographic logic (backtracking between cities/neighborhoods, unrealistic same-day travel times), and trip-level balance (interests represented unevenly, e.g. all food no sights; a lodging gap left unfilled near the trip). Returns plain-language feedback the traveler can act on, not more candidates to choose from. Likely a new agent (not research.py's per-gap agent) since it reasons over the full itinerary at once; needs its own cost tracking like research jobs (see travelplanner-63y).
acceptance_criteria: A 'Review my plan' button on the board triggers a review job; traveler sees plain-language feedback covering pacing, geography, and balance; cost is tracked like other agent jobs.

title: Feed card perks into research and show perk badges on candidates
description: Part of card-perk research (PRD 11a, travelplanner-dky). For lodging and activity research jobs, pass the trip owner's saved cards into ResearchContext and extend the system prompt so the agent searches for and notes current, dated, public perks (travel portal bookings, dining credits, transfer partners) where plausible -- never inventing one. Store perks in Candidate.payload (no migration needed) and surface them as a distinct 'perks' field on BoardCandidate, shown as a dedicated badge (not folded into pros/cons) with 'may apply' wording and a dated source.
acceptance_criteria: Lodging/activity research jobs pass user_cards to the agent when the trip owner has saved cards; perk badges appear on the board distinct from pros/cons with a dated source and 'may apply' wording; no perks are fabricated without a source.
close_reason: Implemented: ResearchContext.user_cards (populated from the trip owner's saved cards for lodging/activity gaps only), PerkIn/perks on CandidateIn + submit_candidates schema, system prompt guidance to search for and note real dated perks (never guess), verify_sources drops any perk without a seen source. Worker stamps a checked_date and saves perks in Candidate.payload (no migration needed). Board exposes BoardCandidate.perks; CandidateCard renders a dedicated perk badge with 'may apply' wording, card name, dated check, and a source link. Verified rendering live in the browser with a seeded candidate.

title: First-time board nudge to add cards
description: Part of card-perk research (PRD 11a, travelplanner-dky). The first time a trip's board has an open lodging or activity gap and the user has never set up cards, show a dismissible banner inviting them to add cards/loyalty programs, linking to the same dialog as the settings entry point. Dismissal should stick (shown once).
acceptance_criteria: Banner appears once per user on a board with an open lodging/activity gap when they have no saved cards; dismissing it persists and it does not reappear.
close_reason: Implemented: User.cards_banner_dismissed flag + migration, POST /me/cards/dismiss-nudge, Board.show_cards_nudge (no cards + open lodging/activity gap + not dismissed), dismissible banner on TripBoard linking to the same CardsDialog via a shared useCardsDialog hook (also refactored into TopBar). Verified end-to-end in the browser: shows, hides on adding cards, dismissal persists across reload.

title: Cards & loyalty settings dialog
description: Part of card-perk research (PRD 11a, travelplanner-dky). A 'Cards & loyalty' entry point in TopBar opening a dialog (styled like CollaboratorsDialog) where a user checks cards/programs from the catalog, plus an 'Other' free-text field, backed by GET/PUT /me/cards.
acceptance_criteria: TopBar has a Cards & loyalty entry; dialog lists the catalog as checkboxes, supports free-text 'Other' entries, and saves via /me/cards.
close_reason: Implemented: CardsDialog component (catalog checkboxes + free-text 'Other' with removable chips), wired into TopBar as a 'Cards & loyalty' entry point available on every page, backed by GET/PUT /me/cards. Verified in browser: loads, saves, and persists across reload.

title: Store a traveler's cards and loyalty programs
description: Foundation for card-perk research (PRD 11a, travelplanner-dky). Add a UserCard table (user_id, card_name) and a small hand-maintained card/loyalty-program catalog module. Names only, no account access. Expose GET/PUT /me/cards (replace-all list, like the existing trip interests pattern).
acceptance_criteria: UserCard model + migration exist; card catalog constant lists major cards/loyalty programs; GET and PUT /me/cards work and are covered by tests.
close_reason: Implemented: UserCard model + migration, card catalog constant, GET /cards/catalog, GET/PUT /me/cards (replace-all, trimmed/deduped, max 30).

title: Show intake chat on the trip board; continue it to edit days
description: Follow-up to travelplanner-5wd (intake sessions are now saved and linked to their trip). Not yet done: showing 'How this trip started' on the board from the linked IntakeSession, and letting the traveler continue that same conversation from the board to change days (e.g. 'add a night in Évora').

title: Send an actual email when someone is invited to a trip
description: Today inviting a collaborator by email just saves the address; nobody is notified. The owner has to tell the invitee themselves, out of band, to go sign in. Needs a transactional email provider (e.g. Resend or Postmark), a from-address/domain, a simple template ('X invited you to help plan Y — sign in at <link> with this email to get access'), and safe local/test behavior (never send real email from tests; log or use a sandbox mode in dev). Related: travelplanner-8me (collaborators).

title: next_sort_order groups only by day, not by time of day
description: app/planning.py's next_sort_order(session, day_id) computes max(sort_order)+1 across the whole day, but callers use it expecting 'last in this part of the day' (see comments in plans.py's update_plan and add_plan). Predates the day-editing feature but that feature's move+change-time-of-day path exercises it more. Not currently causing a visible bug because ordered_day_plans sorts by (time_rank, sort_order) so display order is still correct; only the literal sort_order values interleave across time-of-day groups. Worth fixing if sort_order is ever used directly (e.g. a future drag-to-reorder) instead of always going through the sort.
close_reason: Fixed and deployed 2026-09-17. next_sort_order now takes a time_of_day param and groups by it.

title: Add co-collaborators to trip planning
description: Invite other people (not just the owner) to view/edit a trip together. TripMember table already supports owner|editor|viewer roles and multiple members per trip; today only the owner is ever added (at trip creation). Needs: an invite flow (by email, tied to Clerk accounts), UI to see/manage collaborators, and deciding which actions stay owner-only (delete, restore, share link management) vs open to editors.
close_reason: Merged and deployed 2026-09-17. Invite by email, immediate add if the invitee has an account, pending invite redeemed automatically on first sign-in otherwise. Full edit access via existing membership checks; delete/restore/share stay owner-only.

title: Full day-level editing after the itinerary is planned
description: Once an itinerary is laid out, users should be able to edit each day directly: rename the day and change its contents (add, remove, reorder or move items) without starting the planning over. Today a day is effectively fixed once planned.
close_reason: Merged and deployed 2026-09-17. Day rename plus move-to-day for plans and transit.

title: Save intake chat history
description:
Today the intake conversation lives only in the browser: refreshing /trips/new loses the chat and draft, and after confirm the conversation is gone. Save it.

Scope ideas:
- IntakeSession table (id, user_id, trip_id nullable, messages JSON with role/content/kind, current_draft JSON, created_at, updated_at). Created on first send, updated each turn.
- /trips/new resumes the user's latest unconfirmed session after a refresh; offer 'Start over'.
- On confirm, link the session to the new trip; show 'How this trip started' on the board.
- Later: continue the conversation from the board to change days ('add a night in Évora').
- Delete sessions with their trip; expire unconfirmed sessions after N days.
Keep /intake/turn stateless-compatible (server stores what the client sends) so tests and the agent don't change much.
close_reason: Implemented: IntakeSession table, resume-on-refresh, start-over, link on confirm, expire after 14 days, delete with trip

title: Loyalty and card perks context for the research agent
description: PRD 11a. Traveler-level card/loyalty program list, surfaced via a settings dialog and a one-time board nudge, feeds the research agent for lodging and activity gaps so it can badge candidates where a perk may apply. Dated source per badge, 'may apply' wording, no account access, no redemption. Broken into sub-issues; see deps.
close_reason: All 4 sub-issues shipped: card storage, settings dialog, board nudge, and research pipeline with perk badges.

title: README: add a demo section with screenshots/GIFs
description: README.md is purely dev-setup docs right now (layout table, local dev, deploy steps) -- no visuals, no sense of what the product actually looks or feels like. Add a 'Demo' section near the top, before the Layout table, with a few GIFs or screenshots of the real flow: intake chat -> generated skeleton -> board with a gap -> comparing researched candidates -> a filled-in day -> the public share link. Could reuse the same trip data from manual/browser testing sessions rather than staging a fake one. Keep it short -- this is a look-and-feel hook, not documentation; the existing sections already cover the how.
acceptance_criteria: README has a demo section with at least 2-3 visuals showing the actual app, placed before the technical setup sections.

title: Blog post: insights from building this with an AI agent
description:
Write a blog post about building Trip Planner. Not code work; tracked here so the idea and candidate insights persist across sessions.

Candidate insights surfaced so far, to pick from and sharpen:
- Anti-hallucination as an architectural constraint, not a prompt: verify_sources (app/agents/research.py) throws away any citation the model didn't actually see in its own search results, rather than trusting it to cite honestly. Same pattern extended to card perks -- an unsourced perk claim is dropped entirely, never shown 'unverified.'
- 'Gaps' as the one abstraction everything hangs off: lodging, activities, and (later) transit are all just gaps to fill, with candidates proposed and chosen the same way regardless of kind. Made the card-perks feature, a completely different domain, slot into the existing research pipeline with no new concepts.
- The AI is never the sole source of truth: intake produces an editable draft, not a finished trip; candidates are proposals the traveler chooses or rejects with a reason (which feeds back into the next search). Every AI output is a starting point a human can overwrite.
- Product exploration before code, on a feature with real ambiguity (loyalty cards): walked through where data lives, how it's entered, and where it surfaces before writing a line, and the resulting design was smaller and cleaner than a first guess would've been.
- Cost is a first-class field from day one (ResearchJob.input_tokens/output_tokens/search_count/cost_usd), not bolted on later -- treating agent calls as a metered resource shaped the research prompt itself (search budget, effort level tuned against real cost).
- Dogfooding caught what review didn't: the lodging 'N to fill' miscount (per-day gap attribution using day_id instead of covers_day_ids) was only found by actually clicking through the app, not by reading the diff.
- Speed: ~54 commits from empty repo to a working multi-feature app in about a day and a half of wall-clock time, solo, with an AI agent doing most of the typing -- worth being honest about what that pace does and doesn't prove.

Holly: keep adding insights here as they come up while building, so there's real material by the time this gets written.
notes:
More candidate insights (Claude's observations from working across the codebase this session):

- Inconsistent confidence-handling is intentional, not sloppy: an unsourced lodging/activity candidate is still SHOWN, just labeled "Unverified" -- the human judges it. An unsourced card perk is DROPPED entirely, never shown even flagged. Same underlying mechanism (verify_sources), opposite policy, because the downside is different: a bad restaurant suggestion is annoying, a false promise about a financial benefit is worse. The code encodes a risk calculus per claim-type rather than one global confidence bar.
- No ORM relationships anywhere (FKs declared, never traversed) -- an explicit trade of automatic cascade/relationship-loading for hand-written flush() ordering on every multi-table write. Most frameworks push you toward relationships by default; this one opts out on purpose, and the test suite (SQLite with PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON) is configured specifically to catch the one bug class that trade invites: wrong insert/delete order.
- The intake agent has an explicit patience budget: max 2 follow-up questions, then it's forced to draft with stated assumptions rather than keep asking. Bounding an agent's tolerance for uncertainty, instead of letting it chase certainty indefinitely, so an editable wrong guess ships instead of an interrogation.
- Beads (the issue tracker) is itself git-synced Dolt data living in this repo -- so an AI agent's task list survives across sessions independent of chat history, claimable/updatable by the agent itself, reviewable in the same diffs as the code. Effectively persistent long-term memory for "what's left," decoupled from any one conversation.
- Statelessness was preserved while retrofitting durability: /intake/turn still works with zero server-side state (client sends full history each call) even after IntakeSession persistence was added later -- the server just also saves what it's handed, rather than requiring session state to function. Durability layered on without breaking the original contract or forcing a rewrite.
- Cost-consciousness shows up in control flow, not just pricing math: dismissing a "Find ideas" request specifically cancels its still-queued research job so an unwanted call never runs; the intake question cap exists partly so a conversation doesn't spin billable turns. Unit economics treated as a design constraint from the first commit, not bolted on later.
- Soft-delete-then-sweep is one pattern reused everywhere destructive-ish state needs to happen safely: trashed trips, dismissed requests, unconfirmed intake sessions all mark themselves now and get swept for real by the same background worker loop later, rather than each feature inventing its own cleanup story.
Correction to the earlier "no ORM relationships, on purpose" note: no evidence it was a deliberated trade-off. It's the plain default for a lean SQLModel schema (Field(foreign_key=...) without adding Relationship()/back_populates), present from the very first scaffold commit with no comment explaining why. What IS real and worth keeping: the consequence became a genuinely enforced constraint later -- manual flush() ordering on every multi-table write, and a SQLite test setup (PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON) built specifically to catch violations of it before Postgres would. Worth being honest in the post about which insights are "we chose this for a reason" vs. "this is what stuck from the first commit and got reinforced by tests after the fact."

title: Point a hollyafrench.com subdomain at the Render deploy
description:
Serve the app from Holly's domain instead of onrender.com. Suggested: web at trips.hollyafrench.com, API at trips-api.hollyafrench.com.

Steps:
1. Render: travelplanner-web -> Settings -> Custom Domains -> add trips.hollyafrench.com. travelplanner-api -> add trips-api.hollyafrench.com. Note the DNS target Render shows for each.
2. At the DNS provider for hollyafrench.com (TBD which), add CNAME trips -> travelplanner-web.onrender.com and CNAME trips-api -> travelplanner-api-vfwt.onrender.com (use Render's exact targets). If Cloudflare, set DNS only (grey cloud) until verified.
3. Render: click Verify on both; HTTPS certs are automatic.
4. API env CORS_ORIGINS=https://trips.hollyafrench.com,https://travelplanner-web.onrender.com. Web env VITE_API_URL=https://trips-api.hollyafrench.com, then Manual Deploy the web (build-time var).
5. Verify: https://trips-api.hollyafrench.com/health, sign in at https://trips.hollyafrench.com, create a trip, pins show.
Later/optional: production Clerk instance on hollyafrench.com to remove the dev banner (extra DNS records + new keys).
